name: Filing and paying income tax as a self-employed person or sole proprietor
summary: What a person trading in their own name owes GRA each year, when the return and the four instalments are due, and how to file them.
aliases: how can I pay taxes as a business owner
how do I pay tax on my business
I get shop, how I go pay tax
paying tax as a sole proprietor
how do I file my income tax return
annual tax return for my business
I dey do business, wetin I go pay give GRA
how much tax do I pay on my business
do I have to pay tax on my business

eligibility.text: You must pay income tax if you are an employee, a sole proprietor or a person in partnership and you earn income above GH¢490 per month.
This is the route for a business you own personally - a business name, a sole proprietorship, or trading in your own name. The business and you are the same taxpayer.
If your business is a registered limited company, the company is a separate taxpayer and files corporate income tax instead. You would still file personally on anything you draw from it.
You need a Taxpayer Identification Number before you can file. For individuals this is the PIN on your Ghana Card.

Very small informal operators - dressmakers, hairdressers, barbers, susu collectors, chop bar owners, food sellers, butchers, kiosk and table-top operators, garage owners and artisans - may instead buy the Income Tax Stamp.

documents.name: Your TIN or Ghana Card PIN
documents.where_to_obtain: GRA, or the PIN already printed on your Ghana Card

documents.name: Your business records for the year - sales, purchases, expenses
documents.where_to_obtain: Your own books
documents.note: Chargeable income is worked out from these. GRA does not publish a prescribed format for a small trader's records.

documents.name: Form DT 0103, Personal Income Tax Return
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal, or any GRA Taxpayer Service Centre

documents.name: Form DT 0104, Personal Income Tax Self-Assessment Estimate
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal, or any GRA Taxpayer Service Centre
documents.note: Your own estimate of what you expect to owe for the year ahead. It is what the four instalments are calculated from.

documents.name: Form DT 0104A, Revised Self-Assessment Estimate
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
documents.note: Only if your estimate turns out to be wrong during the year.

documents.name: A Taxpayers Portal account
documents.where_to_obtain: taxpayersportal.com
documents.note: Not required - you can file at a Taxpayer Service Centre - but it is the channel GRA points at first.

steps.action: Register for tax if you have not already, so you have a TIN or a Ghana Card PIN linked to your business
steps.location: taxpayersportal.com or a GRA Taxpayer Service Centre

steps.action: Submit your self-assessment estimate for the year, on Form DT 0104, by the date the first quarterly instalment is due
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
steps.note: If you do not submit an estimate, the Commissioner-General may raise an assessment on you using best judgment - a figure you did not choose.

steps.action: Pay the tax in four quarterly instalments across the year
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal, the GRA mobile app, or a GRA office

steps.action: Keep your records as you go - the annual return is built from them
File the annual return on Form DT 0103 within four months of the year end, and pay anything still outstanding
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA Taxpayer Service Centre

fees.label: Income tax owed
fees.amount_text: Graduated - the first GH¢490 a month is taxed at 0%
fees.note: Above that the rate rises in bands with income. GRA publishes a calculator; the amount depends entirely on your chargeable income, so no single figure exists.

fees.label: Penalty for filing the return late
fees.amount_text: 500 currency points, and a further 10 currency points for each day the failure continues
fees.note: GRA states the penalty in currency points rather than cedis. Ask GRA what a currency point is worth before assuming a cedi figure.

fees.label: Penalty for not paying by the due date
fees.amount_text: A fine set in penalty units, and in some cases imprisonment
fees.note: The range depends on how much tax is involved. See the offences page for the bands.

fees.label: Filing a return
fees.note: GRA charges nothing to file. What you pay is the tax itself.

timeline.standard: Annual return: not later than four months after the end of the year. For a 31 December year end that is 30 April.
timeline.note: The four instalments fall due through the year - see the corporate quarters, which GRA publishes explicitly. GRA does not publish an equivalent dated list for individuals.

rejection_causes.text: Filing without a TIN or Ghana Card PIN linked to the business.
Not submitting a self-assessment estimate, and then being assessed on the Commissioner-General's best judgment instead of your own figures.
Records that do not support the figures on the return.
Treating the four instalments as optional and paying everything at the year end.

caveats.text: This sets out what GRA requires and when. It is not tax advice: how much you owe depends on your own figures, and what is deductible against them is a question for a tax practitioner, not for us.

GRA publishes the four-month annual deadline and the corporate quarterly dates, but does not publish a dated instalment calendar for individuals in the same place. Confirm your instalment dates with your Taxpayer Service Centre.

name: Filing and paying corporate income tax for a limited company
summary: What a registered company owes GRA on its profits, the four quarterly instalment dates GRA publishes, and how the annual return is filed.
aliases: how does my company pay tax

eligibility.text: Every registered company must file its annual returns for each year of assessment.
This applies to companies incorporated in Ghana and to companies incorporated elsewhere that have Ghanaian operations.
A company is a separate taxpayer from its owners. Money you draw out of it is taxed on you separately.
This is not the same as the annual return you file at the Office of the Registrar of Companies. Both exist, they go to different institutions, and doing one does not do the other.

documents.name: The company's TIN
documents.where_to_obtain: GRA

documents.name: Financial statements for the year of assessment
documents.where_to_obtain: Your accountant or auditor

documents.name: Self-assessment estimate of the year's tax
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
documents.note: All businesses are required to submit a tax estimate for the year.

documents.name: A Taxpayers Portal account
documents.where_to_obtain: taxpayersportal.com

steps.action: Submit the company's self-assessment estimate for the year, by the due date of the first quarterly instalment
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a DTRD Taxpayer Service Centre

steps.action: Pay the first instalment on or before 31 March
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: Pay the second instalment on or before 30 June
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: Pay the third instalment on or before 30 September
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: Pay the fourth instalment on or before 31 December
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: File the annual return within four months of the year end, either at a DTRD Taxpayer Service Centre or electronically through the Taxpayers Portal
steps.location: DTRD Taxpayer Service Centre or Taxpayers Portal

fees.label: General corporate income tax rate
fees.note: GRA states rates vary by industry and location, from 5% to 35%. 25% is the general rate.

fees.label: Penalty for filing the return late
fees.amount_text: 500 currency points, and a further 10 currency points for each day the failure continues

timeline.standard: Annual return: not later than four months after the end of the year. Instalments: 31 March, 30 June, 30 September and 31 December.
timeline.note: The quarterly dates above are GRA's own, quoted from the corporate income tax page.

rejection_causes.text: Confusing the GRA tax return with the Registrar of Companies annual return. They are different filings to different institutions.
Missing a quarterly instalment and treating the annual return as the only obligation.
Not submitting a self-assessment estimate, and being assessed on best judgment instead.

caveats.text: Which rate applies to your company, and what is deductible, depends on its industry and circumstances. That is a question for a tax practitioner. What is set out here is the process and the dates.

GRA's corporate income tax page publishes the instalment dates but not the annual return deadline. The four-month rule quoted here comes from GRA's domestic tax FAQ, which states it for all taxpayers.

name: PAYE - deducting and filing tax for your employees
summary: The tax an employer deducts from staff wages and pays to GRA on their behalf, and the monthly return that goes with it.
aliases: how do I pay tax for my employees
I get workers, how I go pay dem tax

eligibility.text: PAYE is a tax deducted from an employee's income and is paid by an employer on behalf of the employee.
If you have employees, deducting and remitting PAYE is your obligation as the employer, not theirs.
Income up to GH¢490 a month is taxed at 0%, so an employee earning below that has nothing deducted - but you may still have to file.
PAYE is separate from SSNIT contributions. Having done one does not do the other.

documents.name: Your TIN as an employer
documents.where_to_obtain: GRA

documents.name: Form DT 0107, Monthly PAYE Deductions Return
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

documents.name: Form DT 0107A, Employer's Monthly PAYE Tax Deductions Schedule
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

documents.name: Form DT 0107C, Disengaged Employees Schedule
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
documents.note: Only where staff have left during the period.

documents.name: Form DT 0108, Annual PAYE Deductions Return
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
documents.note: The annual return, with schedules DT 0108A and DT 0108B.

documents.name: Payroll records for each employee
documents.where_to_obtain: Your own records

steps.action: Deduct tax from each employee's pay every month, using the graduated rates
File the monthly PAYE return with its schedule, on or before the fifteenth day of the month following the month in which the deduction was made
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: Pay the deducted tax to GRA by the same fifteenth-day deadline
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal, the GRA app, or a GRA office

steps.action: File the annual PAYE return with its employee schedules after the year end
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

fees.label: What you deduct from each employee
fees.amount_text: Graduated — 0% on the first GH¢490 a month, rising to 35%
fees.note: The exact deduction depends on the employee's pay. GRA publishes a PAYE calculator; the bands are listed below.

fees.label: Top band
fees.note: The bands between are graduated. GRA publishes a PAYE calculator.

fees.label: Penalty for filing late
fees.amount_text: 500 currency points, and a further 10 currency points for each day the failure continues

timeline.standard: Monthly: on or before the fifteenth day of the month following the deduction.
timeline.note: GRA's tax calendar lists the 15th of each month for PAYE and withholding taxes.

rejection_causes.text: Filing the return but not remitting the money, or the other way round. Both are due on the 15th.
Submitting the return without the employee schedule.
Assuming staff below the tax-free threshold mean nothing has to be filed.

caveats.text: The rate bands quoted here are the ones GRA published for 2024 on its PAYE page. Bands are revised in the annual budget - check the current year's rates before running payroll on them.

name: Filing your monthly VAT return
summary: What a VAT-registered business files each month, when it is due, and what the rate and levies add up to under the 2026 VAT Act.
aliases: I need to file VAT returns
charging VAT and paying it over
when do I pay my VAT
keywords: last working day of the month

eligibility.text: Every VAT-registered business must file a return each month, whether or not it made any taxable supplies in that month.
If you are not yet registered, registration comes first - the thresholds changed on 1 January 2026 under Act 1151.
The VAT Flat Rate Scheme has been abolished, so a business that used to file under it now files at the standard rate.

documents.name: Your VAT registration and TIN
documents.where_to_obtain: GRA

documents.name: Records of taxable supplies made and received in the month
documents.where_to_obtain: Your own books

documents.name: VAT Standard Rate Return
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

documents.name: NHIL, GETFund Levy and COVID-19 Levy Return
documents.where_to_obtain: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office
documents.note: GRA lists this as a return type alongside the VAT return. The COVID-19 levy itself was abolished from 1 January 2026.

steps.action: Charge VAT and the levies on your taxable supplies through the month, and keep the records
File the return by the last working day of the month immediately following the month the return relates to
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal or a GRA office

steps.action: Pay what is due by the same deadline
steps.location: Taxpayers Portal, the GRA app, or a GRA office

fees.label: COVID-19 Health Recovery Levy
fees.note: The 1% levy has been abolished under the 2026 reforms.

fees.label: Penalty for filing late
fees.amount_text: 500 currency points, and a further 10 currency points for each day the failure continues

timeline.standard: Monthly: by the last working day of the month immediately following the month to which the return relates.

rejection_causes.text: Not filing in a month with no sales. The return is still due.
Still filing under the flat rate scheme, which no longer exists.
Treating the last working day as the last calendar day when the month ends at a weekend.

caveats.text: VAT changed substantially on 1 January 2026 under Act 1151: the flat rate scheme was removed, the COVID-19 levy abolished and the goods threshold raised. Any guide written before that date is describing a system that no longer exists.

name: Income Tax Stamp for small informal-sector businesses
summary: The simplified route GRA offers small operators in the informal sector instead of filing a full income tax return.
aliases: I be hairdresser, wetin I go pay

eligibility.text: The Income Tax Stamp is designed for individuals operating in the informal sector, for example small-scale self-employed dressmakers and tailors, hairdressers, beauticians and barbers, susu collectors, chop bar owners, cooked food sellers, butchers, container, kiosk and table-top operators, garage owners and artisans.

documents.name: Identification
documents.where_to_obtain: Your Ghana Card

steps.action: Ask at your nearest GRA Taxpayer Service Centre which stamp applies to your trade and what it costs

fees.label: Cost of the stamp
fees.note: GRA's FAQ describes who the stamp is for but does not publish the amounts, which vary by trade and by locality. Ask at a Taxpayer Service Centre.

timeline.note: GRA does not publish a purchase cycle on the page we can cite.

caveats.text: This is the thinnest card in our knowledge base. GRA names the trades the stamp is for, but publishes no rate table or process we could find on an official page. Everything beyond who it applies to should be confirmed at a Taxpayer Service Centre before you rely on it.
